NOTE: the same wedge as dump-wedged.txt, but with the RPC pool threads named by the
engine-host's own ThreadFactory instead of the JDK default. This is what the image
emits once the factory is named, so it is the shape the watchdog must recognise from
then on. All 8 are blocked and the holder (HTTP-Dispatcher) is outside the pool, so
it MUST fire.

KILLS: dropping the authoritative `engine-rpc-<n>` name shape and keeping only the
`pool-<n>-thread-<m>` fallback. That predicate sees zero pool threads here, reports
"no RPC pool threads found", and never recovers a real deadlock.
